description: Dysprosium is a chemical element with symbol Dy and atomic number 66. It is a rare-earth element in the lanthanide series with a metallic silver luster. It is never found in nature as a free element but is found in various minerals such as xenotime.
uses: Dysprosium is used to produce neodymium-iron-boron magnets crucial for electric vehicle motors and wind turbines. It is used for its high thermal neutron absorption cross-section in control rods in nuclear reactors, for its high magnetic susceptibility in data-storage applications, and as a component of Terfenol-D, a magnetostrictive material. It is also used in laser materials, commercial lighting, infrared radiation sources, dosimeters, and nanofibers for reinforcement and catalysis.
characteristics: Dysprosium has a bright metallic silver luster and is soft, capable of being machined without sparking if overheating is avoided. It has the highest magnetic strength of the elements, especially at low temperatures, with a Curie temperature of 90.5 K. Its physical characteristics can be greatly affected by even small amounts of impurities, and soluble dysprosium salts are mildly toxic while insoluble salts are considered non-toxic.
